exact_statement: Let A=(g+h)/2,V=(g-h)/2,F=A+iV for an actual Boolean split, u=Ahat,v=Vhat,d=Inf_i, and M_i be the mutual information of the spectral-sector law with masses u_T^2,v_T^2. Full Booleanity gives F^4=1 and I(F^2)/2=W_i=2 sum_(U nonempty)|U|(sum_T v_T v_(T xor U))^2. With R_i=W_i-d log2(1/d)>=0 and sigma(d)=log2(e)d-(1-d)log2(1/(1-d))>=0, B_i=W_i+log2(e)d-R_i-M_i-sigma(d). In particular B_i+M_i<=W_i+log2(e)d; this bound fails for the normalized non-Boolean coefficient vector (4/5,3/5). In any bound B_i<=alpha I(F^2)+C d valid for all Boolean splits with fixed finite C, necessarily alpha>=1/2, as witnessed by even-dimensional bent one-point phase surgery.
hypotheses: Genuine Boolean sign on a finite uniform cube
Entropy in bits; all zero and deterministic-sector conventions in PHASE_ERASURE.md
refutes: universal coordinate bound B_i<=alpha I(F^2)+C d with alpha<1/2
admission of arbitrary normalized real vectors to the phase boundary inequality

exact_statement: For every even r>=2, the Boolean sign f_r(x,y)=(-1)^(x^T(I_r+J_r)y) has flat spectrum, H=2r,I=r,B_i=1,d_i=1/2,M_i=0,W_i=(r-1)/2,R_i=(r-2)/2 for every coordinate. Hence Q_sum=sum_i W_i=r(r-1) and (Q_sum-a sum_i M_i)/I=r-1 for any fixed a>=0. No fixed finite K,a>=0 universally satisfy Q_sum-a sum_i M_i<=K I on all Boolean functions. Subtracting the physical deficits gives Q_sum-sum_i(R_i+M_i)=I on this family. This refutation concerns an all-coordinate aggregate and does not refute localized bad-node tree payment.
hypotheses: Genuine Boolean sign on a finite uniform cube

refutes: universal Q_sum-a sum_i M_i<=K I with finite K,a>=0

exact_statement: Let N_odd(f) be the number of 2-faces of {0,1}^n on which f has corner product -1 and Q(f)=2^(1-n) N_odd(f). exact_statement: For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign f, let a_S=fhat(S), p_S=a_S^2, ell_S=log2(1/p_S) on positive atoms and a_S ell_S=0 otherwise, c_U=sum_S a_S a_(S xor U) ell_S, E_log=sum_(U nonempty)|U|c_U^2, and J_R=sum_(U nonempty)p_(R xor U)/|U|. Every occupied R obeys p_R[H(f)-ell_R]^2<=J_R E_log; also sum_(U nonempty)c_U^2=Var_p(ell). For a largest atom, H(f)<=ell_R+sqrt(J_R E_log/p_R).

exact_statement: There is no finite universal K with E_log(f)<=K I(f), nor any finite universal K with sqrt(J_R E_log(f)/p_R)<=K I(f) for the largest-atom anchor R of every Boolean f. The first is refuted by n-bit one-point defects with E_log/I~4n^2; the second by disjoint tensor powers of the three-bit point defect, whose anchor cost is exponentially large while influence is linear.
